newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-ACT BEAT WELLINGTON TO REACH SUPER 12 FINAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ACT BEAT WELLINGTON TO REACH SUPER 12 FINAL.

text.p: ACT Brumbies extended their winning record at home in Super 12 rugby by defeating Wellington Hurricanes 33-20 in a tense semifinal on Saturday.
The Brumbies earned a trip to Eden Park in New Zealand for an encounter with champions Auckland in next weekend's final after running in five tries to two at Bruce Stadium.
Former Australia test fly-half David Knox advanced his claim for a Wallaby recall with an inspired display in attack as ACT recorded their second win in a week over the Hurricanes.
The 33-year-old veteran capitalised on a steady stream of quick possession from scrum-half George Gregan to direct a succession of inventive raids by the Brumbies' backline.
But although Knox played a pivotal role in attack, he was off target with his kicking, allowing Wellington to stay in the game despite being under intense pressure for long periods.
Knox landed only one conversion and two penalties, missing several other easy attempts, including one directly in front of the posts.
The misses helped Wellington draw level at 13-13 early in the second half before ACT broke clear with two tries in as many minutes from centre James Holbeck and winger Mitch Hardy.
Holbeck scored a second try late in the game to seal ACT's 11th home win in a row since they joined the Super 12 competition last season.
They defeated the Hurricanes in New Zealand last weekend in the final round of the regular season to earn home advantage.
"This is only our second year in the Super 12 and we have reached the final -- it is a magnificent performance," said ACT captain and flanker Brett Robinson.
"But we won't have many friends at Eden Park against Auckland next week so we will have to get it together this week and make sure we concentrate."

ACT's progression to the Super 12 final has proved an embarrassment for their richer compatriots New South Wales and Queensland, the supposed powers in Australian rugby, who both flopped badly this season.
Gregan delighted a crowd of more than 23,000 -- a record for a rugby union match in Canberra -- by rounding off the ACT's first attack of the match with a try near the touchline in the third minute.
Knox produced one of his trademark loop movements with centre Pat Howard to set up winger Joe Roff for a further score in the 22nd minute.
Knox, who missed both conversion attempts, and Wellington scrum-half Jon Preston then traded penalties to give the home side a 13-3 lead at halftime.

Cullen, who scored both Wellington tries, set up a tense finale when he crossed the line with four minutes remaining. Preston kicked two conversions and two penalties to complete his side's points total.
